/--
Let \( D \) be a unique factorization domain.
Prove that if every nonzero prime ideal of \( D \) is maximal, then \( D \) is a principal ideal domain.
-/
theorem isPrincipalIdealRing_of_isPrime_ne_bot_isMaximal {D : Type} [CommRing D] [IsDomain D]
    [UniqueFactorizationMonoid D] (h : ∀ P : Ideal D, [P.IsPrime] → P ≠ ⊥ → P.IsMaximal) : IsPrincipalIdealRing D := by
  have prime_principal : ∀ P : Ideal D, P.IsPrime → P ≠ ⊥ →
      ∃ p : D, P = Ideal.span {p} := by
    intro P hP hPne
    sorry
  have maximal_principal : ∀ M : Ideal D, M.IsMaximal → ∃ m, M = Ideal.span {m} := by
    intro M hM
    by_cases hMb : M = ⊥
    · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
      subst hMb
      rw [Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot.mpr rfl]
    · exact prime_principal M hM.isPrime hMb
  have every_ideal_principal : ∀ I : Ideal D, Submodule.IsPrincipal I := by
    intro I
    by_cases hI : I = ⊥
    · refine ⟨⟨0, ?_⟩⟩
      subst hI
      rw [Submodule.span_zero_singleton]
    · sorry
  exact ⟨fun I => every_ideal_principal I⟩

/-- Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain and $\mathfrak{a} \neq 0$ an ideal in $A$. Show that every ideal in
 $A/\mathfrak{a}$ is principal. -/
theorem isPrincipalIdealRing_quot_of_isDedekind {A : Type} [CommRing A]
    [IsDedekindDomain A] (a : Ideal A) (ha : a ≠ ⊥) :
    IsPrincipalIdealRing (A ⧸ a) := by
  -- Bridge lemma: every ideal `b ⊇ a` is of the form `span {y} ⊔ a`.
  have bridge : ∀ (b : Ideal A), a ≤ b → ∃ y : A, b = Ideal.span {y} ⊔ a := by
    sorry
  -- Reduction: every ideal of `A ⧸ a` comes from an ideal of `A` containing `a`.
  refine ⟨fun J => ?_⟩
  -- Pull `J` back to an ideal `b` of `A` containing `a`.
  set b : Ideal A := J.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) with hb_def
  have hab : a ≤ b := by
    intro x hx
    show (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) x ∈ J
    have : (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) x = 0 := Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hx
    rw [this]
    exact J.zero_mem
  have hbmap : b.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) = J := by
    rw [hb_def]
    exact Ideal.map_comap_of_surjective _ Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective J
  -- Apply the bridge lemma.
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := bridge b hab
  refine ⟨⟨(Ideal.Quotient.mk a) y, ?_⟩⟩
  -- Now compute `J` from `b = span {y} ⊔ a`.
  have hJ : J = (Ideal.span {y} ⊔ a).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) := by
    rw [← hbmap, hy]
  have hmap_sup : (Ideal.span {y} ⊔ a).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)
      = (Ideal.span {y}).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) ⊔ a.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) :=
    Ideal.map_sup _ _ _
  have ha_map : a.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) = ⊥ := by
    rw [Ideal.map_quotient_self]
  have hspan : (Ideal.span {y}).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)
      = Ideal.span {(Ideal.Quotient.mk a) y} := by
    rw [Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton]
  rw [hJ, hmap_sup, ha_map, hspan, sup_bot_eq]
  rfl

/-- Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $\mathfrak{a}, \mathfrak{b}$ be ideals in $A$. If $M$ is
any $A$-module, let $M_{\mathfrak{a}}$, $M_{\mathfrak{b}}$ denote its $\mathfrak{a}$-adic and
$\mathfrak{b}$-adic completions respectively. If $M$ is finitely generated, prove that
$(M_{\mathfrak{a}})_{\mathfrak{b}} \cong M_{\mathfrak{a} + \mathfrak{b}}$. -/
theorem nonempty_adicCompletion_adicCompletion_linearEquiv {A M : Type} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (𝒜 : Ideal A) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (ℬ : Ideal A) :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion ℬ (AdicCompletion 𝒜 M) ≃ₗ[A] AdicCompletion (𝒜 + ℬ) M) := by
  have h1 : ∀ n : ℕ, 𝒜 ^ n ≤ (𝒜 + ℬ) ^ n := by
    intro n
    exact Ideal.pow_le_pow_left le_sup_left n
  have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, ℬ ^ n ≤ (𝒜 + ℬ) ^ n := by
    intro n
    exact Ideal.pow_le_pow_left le_sup_right n
  have hf : Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion ℬ (AdicCompletion 𝒜 M) →ₗ[A] AdicCompletion (𝒜 + ℬ) M) := by
    exact Classical.choice inferInstance
  have hg : Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (𝒜 + ℬ) M →ₗ[A] AdicCompletion ℬ (AdicCompletion 𝒜 M)) := by
    exact Classical.choice inferInstance
  obtain ⟨f⟩ := hf
  obtain ⟨g⟩ := hg
  exact ⟨LinearEquiv.ofLinear f g (by ext x; rfl) (by ext x; rfl)⟩

/-- Let $M$ be an $R$-module. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $M$ is finitely generated.
    \item For every family $(Q_{\alpha})_{\alpha \in A}$ of $R$-modules, the canonical map
    $M \otimes_{R} \left( \prod_{\alpha} Q_{\alpha} \right) \to \prod_{\alpha} (M \otimes_{R}
    Q_{\alpha})$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate} -/
theorem finite_iff_surjective_linearMap {R : Type} [CommRing R]
    (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Finite R M ↔ ∀ {α : Type} (Q : α → Type),
    ∀ [(a : α) → AddCommGroup (Q a)] [(a : α) → Module R (Q a)],
        Function.Surjective (LinearMap.pi (
            fun i => LinearMap.lTensor M (
                LinearMap.proj i (φ := Q) (R := R)))) := by
  sorry

/--
Suppose that \( R \) is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal \( \mathfrak{m} \) and residue field \( \kappa \).
In this case the projective dimension of \( \kappa \) is \( \geq \dim_{\kappa} \mathfrak{m} / \mathfrak{m}^{2} \).-/
theorem not_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_finrank_cotangentSpace {R : Type} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] :
      ¬ CategoryTheory.HasProjectiveDimensionLT
        (ModuleCat.of R (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R))
          (Module.finrank (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace R)) := by
  intro h
  -- Set up notation
  set κ := IsLocalRing.ResidueField R
  set n := Module.finrank κ (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace R)
  -- Step 1: From projective dimension bound, derive vanishing of Tor at degree n.
  have hTorVanish :
      ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{0} R),
        IsZero ((Tor R n).obj (ModuleCat.of R κ) |>.obj M) := by
    sorry
  -- Step 2: Tor_n^R(κ, κ) is isomorphic (as κ-vector space) to the n-th exterior
  -- power of the cotangent space, which has positive κ-dimension when n equals
  -- the embedding dimension.
  have hTorNonzero :
      ¬ IsZero ((Tor R n).obj (ModuleCat.of R κ) |>.obj (ModuleCat.of R κ)) := by
    sorry
  -- Step 3: Derive contradiction.
  have hZero : IsZero ((Tor R n).obj (ModuleCat.of R κ) |>.obj (ModuleCat.of R κ)) :=
    hTorVanish (ModuleCat.of R κ)
  exact hTorNonzero hZero

/--
Let \( R \) be a Dedekind domain. Show the following:
If \( P_1, \dots, P_n \in \operatorname{Spec}(R) \) are pairwise distinct, non-zero prime ideals
and \( e_1, \dots, e_n \) are non-negative integers, there exists \( a \in R \setminus \{0\} \) such that
\[
(a) = P_1^{e_1} \cdots P_n^{e_n} \cdot J,
\]
with \( J \subseteq R \) an ideal in whose factorization none of the \( P_i \) appear.
-/
theorem exists_factor_principal_ideal (R : Type) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R]
    (n : ℕ) (p : (Fin n) → PrimeSpectrum R) (h_nonzero : ∀ i, (p i).asIdeal ≠ ⊥)
    (h_inj : Function.Injective p) (e : (Fin n) → ℕ) :
    ∃ (a : R) (J : Ideal R), a ≠ 0 ∧ Ideal.span {a} = J * ∏ (i : Fin n), (p i).1 ^ (e i) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin n), ¬ ∃ (K : Ideal R), J = K * (p i).1) := by
  -- Set Q to be the product ideal
  set Q : Ideal R := ∏ i : Fin n, (p i).1 ^ (e i) with hQ
  -- Step 1: Q is nonzero
  have hQ_ne : Q ≠ ⊥ := by
    rw [hQ]
    exact Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr (fun i _ => pow_ne_zero _ (h_nonzero i))
  -- Step 2: pick a nonzero element of Q
  have hex : ∃ a : R, a ∈ Q ∧ a ≠ 0 := by
    exact (Submodule.ne_bot_iff Q).mp hQ_ne
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀_mem, ha₀_ne⟩ := hex
  -- Step 3: Q divides span {a₀}
  have hI_ne : Ideal.span {a₀} ≠ ⊥ := by
    rwa [Ne, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot]
  have hdvd : Q ∣ Ideal.span {a₀} := by
    rw [Ideal.dvd_iff_le, Ideal.span_singleton_le_iff_mem]
    exact ha₀_mem
  -- Step 4: extract the cofactor
  obtain ⟨J', hJ'⟩ := hdvd
  -- Step 5: produce the desired witness using J' purified of the P_i's
  refine ⟨a₀, J', ha₀_ne, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- equation: span {a₀} = J' * Q
    rw [hJ']; ring
  · -- the no-P_i condition (left as sorry hole in this decomposition step)
    intro i ⟨K, hK⟩
    sorry

/--Let \( I_1, I_2 \subseteq K[x_1, \dots, x_n] \) be two ideals. With \( y \) an additional
indeterminate, form the ideal
\[
J := \big( y \cdot I_1 \cup (1 - y) \cdot I_2 \big) K[x_1, \dots, x_n, y] \subseteq K[x_1, \dots,
x_n, y].
\]Show that
\[
I_1 \cap I_2 = K[x_1, \dots, x_n] \cap J.
\]-/
theorem inf_eq_span_X_smul_sup_one_sub_X_smul_comap_C {K : Type} [Field K] (n : ℕ) 
    (I1 I2 : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)) :
    I1 ⊓ I2 = (Ideal.span {(X : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)[X])} • (I1.map C) ⊔
    Ideal.span {(1 - X : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)[X])} • (I2.map C) ).comap C := by
  set R := MvPolynomial (Fin n) K
  set J : Ideal R[X] :=
    Ideal.span {(X : R[X])} • (I1.map C) ⊔
    Ideal.span {(1 - X : R[X])} • (I2.map C) with hJ
  -- Key auxiliary: image of I.map C under any eval r lies in I.
  have key : ∀ (I : Ideal R) (r : R) (p : R[X]),
      p ∈ I.map (C : R →+* R[X]) → eval r p ∈ I := by
    intro I r p hp
    have h1 : (I.map (C : R →+* R[X])).map (evalRingHom r) ≤ I := by
      rw [Ideal.map_map]
      intro x hx
      have : (evalRingHom r).comp (C : R →+* R[X]) = RingHom.id R := by
        ext a; simp [evalRingHom]
      rw [this] at hx
      simpa [Ideal.map_id] using hx
    exact h1 (Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hp)
  -- Forward direction
  have fwd : I1 ⊓ I2 ≤ J.comap (C : R →+* R[X]) := by
    intro f hf
    obtain ⟨hf1, hf2⟩ := hf
    show C f ∈ J
    have heq : (C f : R[X]) = X * C f + (1 - X) * C f := by ring
    rw [heq]
    apply Ideal.add_mem
    · apply Ideal.mem_sup_left
      apply Ideal.mul_mem_mul
      · exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _)
      · exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hf1
    · apply Ideal.mem_sup_right
      apply Ideal.mul_mem_mul
      · exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _)
      · exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hf2
  -- Backward direction
  have bwd : J.comap (C : R →+* R[X]) ≤ I1 ⊓ I2 := by
    intro f hf
    have hCf : C f ∈ J := hf
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · -- evaluate at 1
      have hsub : ∀ p ∈ J, eval 1 p ∈ I1 := by
        intro p hp
        refine Submodule.add_induction_of_mem hp ?_ ?_
        all_goals sorry
      have : eval (1 : R) (C f) = f := by simp
      have := hsub (C f) hCf
      simpa [eval_C] using this
    · -- evaluate at 0
      have hsub : ∀ p ∈ J, eval 0 p ∈ I2 := by
        intro p hp
        sorry
      have := hsub (C f) hCf
      simpa [eval_C] using this
  exact le_antisymm fwd bwd
